# Requirements Document: Order versions and history

## Introduction

An order starts at version 1, and each group of changes the airline applies
raises its version by one.  The order's history is the order at version 1
followed by the change groups, from which a seller can rebuild each version.
A seller may send the version it saw with a change, so the airline can tell
whether the change was made on data that still holds.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/Creation/Version.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/verified-air/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/Creation/Version.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-404

**User Story:** As a seller, I want each version of an order to stand for one set of changes, so that I can rebuild any version from the order's history.

**Rule:** WHEN the airline applies a group of changes to an order THE SYSTEM SHALL raise the order's version by one and record the group in the order's history. (Lean: `recordChanges`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN an order is created THE SYSTEM SHALL give it version 1 and a history with no change groups.
   - ONE-404.1, proven: proven theorem `create_version_one`; example `versionsOfTrip`
2. WHEN the airline applies a group of changes to an order THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the group to the order and raise its version by one.
   - ONE-404.2, proven: proven theorem `record_raises_version`; example `versionsOfTrip`
3. THE SYSTEM SHALL keep an order's version one more than the number of change groups applied since it was created.
   - ONE-404.3, proven: proven theorem `version_counts_groups`; example `versionsOfTrip`
4. WHEN a seller asks for an order's history THE SYSTEM SHALL return the order at version 1 and each later change group once, labelled with the version it produced.
   - ONE-404.4, proven: proven theorem `history_lists_each_group`; example `versionsOfTrip`
5. WHEN a seller applies the change groups of an order's history to the order at version 1 in the order listed THE SYSTEM SHALL give the order as it is now.
   - ONE-404.5, open: open theorem `history_rebuilds_current`; counterexample `newestFirstHistory`

#### Open question on ONE-404.5

> Applying the change groups of an order's history to the order at version
> 1, in the order listed, gives the order as it is now, under both readings.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide lists change groups oldest first,
> each raising the version by one, while the capability page for order history
> lists them newest first and says each lowers the version.  Applied newest
> first, a group that removes an item runs before the group that added it, and
> the item comes back.  The example `newestFirstHistory` shows it.  In
> which order does the history list its change groups, and does a history
> requested from version v include the group that produced v?

### Requirement ONE-405

**User Story:** As a seller, I want a change I make on an order I saw at an older version to be refused, so that I never overwrite a change I have not seen.

**Rule:** WHEN a seller sends a change request THE SYSTEM SHALL compare the order version the request carries, if any, with the order's current version before applying the change. (Lean: `requestChange`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a change request carries the order's current version THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the change and raise the version by one.
   - ONE-405.1, proven: proven theorem `current_version_applied`; example `twoSellersOneVersion`
2. WHEN a change request carries no version THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the change.
   - ONE-405.2, proven: proven theorem `no_version_applied`; example `twoSellersOneVersion`
3. IF a change request carries a version other than the order's current version THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the change.
   - ONE-405.3, open: open theorem `stale_rejected`; counterexample `twoSellersOneVersion`

#### Open question on ONE-405.3

> A change that carries a version other than the order's current version is
> rejected, under both readings.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide lets the airline return an error
> when the versions differ and does not require it.  Under the reading where
> the airline applies the change anyway, a seller who saw an older version
> overwrites a change it never saw.  The example `twoSellersOneVersion`
> shows it.  Does a version mismatch always reject the change, and may a change
> be sent without a version?
